sources.entry: 4ga Boards - Straightforward realtime kanban boards management for intuitive task tracking. Featuring an elegant dark mode, collapsible todo lists, and multitasking tools to supercharge your team's productivity. (Demo, Source Code) MIT Nodejs/Docker/K8S

summary.one_liner: 4ga Boards is a self-hostable, realtime kanban-style project management board app with a web UI, built on React and Sails.js with PostgreSQL.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a web app for organizing work in a multi-level hierarchy of projects, boards, lists, cards, and tasks. Changes update in realtime without reloading the page. It includes a dark mode, an advanced Markdown editor, collapsible lists and sidebar, and keyboard shortcuts. Users can export and import boards, and import from Trello is mentioned. Login options listed are Google, GitHub, Microsoft, and OIDC SSO, and the UI is offered in multiple languages. Deployment is documented via Docker Compose (recommended), Kubernetes, TrueNAS, or a manual Node.js setup, along with backup and restore scripts for Docker installs. A GitHub two-way sync is listed as "coming soon".
use_cases: self-hosted kanban board for a team
organizing cards with a Markdown editor
team project management with SSO login
how_to_run: curl -L -o docker-compose.yml (download the compose file; URL not specified in the README)
Edit BASE_URL, SECRET_KEY (openssl rand -hex 64), and POSTGRES_PASSWORD / DATABASE_URL in docker-compose.yml
Development: git clone the repository, then pnpm i
cp server/.env.sample server/.env, then docker compose -f docker-compose-dev.yml up -d
notable: Multitasking: edit or review cards while filtering and rearranging the board, keeping local description changes
Multi-level hierarchy from projects down to tasks
Multiple SSO providers including Google, GitHub, Microsoft, and OIDC
caveats: GitHub two-way sync is listed as coming soon, not yet available
Requires PostgreSQL; the Docker setup depends on a configured database password
Default demo credentials (demo/demo) must be changed for a real deployment; the README does not say so explicitly
